chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Khuzayma ibn Yaqtin, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Bukayr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The origins of the obligatory shares (of inheritance) are from six portions — they do not exceed that, nor is there deficiency/excess (awl) upon them. Then the remaining wealth, after that, belongs to the people of the shares who are mentioned in the Book (Quran).

key_terms.الأسهم: al-asham — the six base shares/portions from which all inheritance fractions derive (common denominator of 6)
key_terms.الفرائض: al-fara'id — the obligatory shares of inheritance, specifically the fixed portions (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/3, 2/3, 1/6) allocated to heirs in the Quran
key_terms.الكتاب: al-Kitab — the Book, referring to the Quran and its inheritance verses in Surah al-Nisa
key_terms.عول: awl — the Sunni doctrine that when designated shares exceed 100%, each heir's portion is proportionally reduced; rejected in Shia jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the basis of inheritance shares in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the foundational principle of Islamic inheritance law: all obligatory shares of inheritance derive from six base portions and cannot exceed this number. The principle of 'awl' — the pro-rata reduction of shares when they collectively exceed the estate — is explicitly rejected. Any remaining wealth after the obligatory shares are distributed returns to the primary heirs designated in the Quran (Surah al-Nisa, 4:11-12), following the Shia principle that rejects awl in favor of radd (return of surplus to heirs).
word_analysis: is deficient/the shares exceed the estate

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya from Khuzayma Bin Yaqteen, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj, from Bukeyr, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:

‘The origins of the obligatory (shares of inheritances) are from six shares, not exceeding upon that, and there is no deficiency/excess to it. Then the wealth, after that, is for the people of the shares which are Mentioned in the Book (Quran)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Khudhaymah ibn Yaqtin from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Bukayr who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The roots of ordained shares are six. They do not increase or face deficiency and thereafter the legacy is for those whose shares are mentioned in the book (of Allah).”’
